n1f7fe729797f: People with pre-existing mental health disorders (PMHD) often have lower cancer screening uptake and later-stage diagnoses. It remains unclear whether these disparities persist within highly accessible universal healthcare systems without strict gatekeeping. We simultaneously investigated the associations between PMHD and both screening participation and stage at diagnosis of breast and bowel cancers within the Taiwan health service. Using nationwide National Health Insurance and Cancer Registry data covering over 99% of the population, we compared outcomes between individuals with and without PMHD. Propensity score matching was applied for the screening cohort. Adjusted odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression, with subgroup analyses for severe PMHD. Overall, PMHD was associated with higher screening participation (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: breast = 1.04, bowel = 1.12) and reduced odds of metastatic disease at diagnosis (breast = 0.72, bowel = 0.93), although the magnitude of these associations was modest, particularly for bowel cancer. Conversely, individuals with severe PMHD had significantly lower odds of screening (breast = 0.81, bowel = 0.88) despite high outpatient use. Furthermore, while the severe group retained reduced odds of metastatic breast cancer at diagnosis (aOR = 0.79), they showed no staging advantage for bowel cancer. While Taiwan’s highly accessible universal healthcare system may contribute to a surveillance effect benefiting the general PMHD population, significant disparities persist for individuals with severe illnesses. Targeted interventions, procedural simplifications for self-administered tests, and multidisciplinary person-centred care models, may be needed to ensure health equity.
n553e18017ac2: Objective The aim of the study was to investigate whether the addition of an erector spinae plane block (ESPB) to surgical intercostal nerve block (INB) provides additional postoperative analgesic benefits in patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). Methods This prospective, randomized controlled trial included 60 adult patients undergoing elective three-port VATS. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either combined ESPB plus INB (EI) or INB alone. Patients, surgeons, ward nurses, postoperative outcome assessors, and data analysts were blinded to group assignment, whereas the anesthesiologists performing the intervention were unblinded. The primary outcome was pain intensity at 1 hour postoperatively, assessed using the Numerical Rating Scale (NRS). Prespecified secondary outcomes included repeated postoperative NRS pain assessments through 48 hours and cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours. Results The NRS pain score at 1 hour postoperatively was 5.83 ± 2.86 in the EI group and 5.52 ± 3.10 in the INB group (mean difference 0.31, 95% confidence interval [CI], −1.25 to 1.87, p = 0.691). In a post hoc exploratory longitudinal analysis, a linear mixed-effects model demonstrated no significant group-by-time interaction in postoperative NRS pain scores (F[7, 401.2] = 0.81, p = 0.581). Cumulative opioid consumption at 24 hours, expressed as intravenous morphine equivalents, was 41.0 mg (interquartile range [IQR], 31.0–58.5) in the EI group and 40.0 mg (IQR, 29.1–48.3) in the INB group (between-group difference, 3.0 mg; 95% CI, −6.2 to 12.0; p = 0.501). Conclusions Adding single-injection ESPB to surgical INB did not significantly reduce 1-hour postoperative pain scores or 24-hour opioid consumption following VATS. Larger adequately powered studies are required to determine whether smaller clinically relevant incremental benefits exist. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03949790
n0ca4bbdcb8eb: by Antonia L. Stengler, Elke Mattern, Ulrich Ronellenfitsch, Anke Steckelberg Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges not only to healthcare systems but also to healthcare professionals. This study explores the experiences, perceptions, and perceived burdens of healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery during the pandemic, with a particular focus on clinical staff working in hospital-based care in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. Methods A qualitative, interpretive-hermeneutic approach was employed using one focus group and one individual semi-structured interview. Participants were healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients undergoing oncological surgery. The focus group included 12 participants, and one additional participant took part in an individual interview. The transcripts were independently coded and analytically annotated by two researchers and systematically analyzed in an iterative process using MAXQDA. The analysis combined deductively informed codes derived from the interview guide with inductively developed codes emerging from the data. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) reporting statement. Results In September 2024, one focus group and one individual interview were conducted with a total of 13 participants, predominantly nurses and nursing assistants. Nine categories were identified. Participants described substantial emotional, professional, and organizational burdens during the COVID-19 pandemic, including stress, anxiety, increased demands, uncertainty, and difficulties in maintaining usual standards of patient care. Participants also reported challenges related to postponed or adapted oncological treatments, communication with patients under infection-control measures, postoperative care under capacity constraints, team collaboration, and the availability and use of personal protective equipment. Political measures, changing regulations, and the occupational vaccination mandate were perceived by participants as sources of uncertainty, frustration, and reduced autonomy. Despite these challenges, participants also described experiences of team cohesion and professional commitment. Participants expressed a need for clearer guidance, accessible contact persons, psychosocial support, supervision, and greater involvement in decision-making. Conclusion The findings suggest that healthcare professionals involved in hospital-based oncological surgical care experienced substantial emotional, ethical, and organizational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants’ accounts indicate that pandemic preparedness should extend beyond infection control and include clear communication, consistent guidance, psychosocial support, supervision, and adequate organizational resources. Given the small, convenience-based, and predominantly nursing sample, these findings should be interpreted as context-specific accounts rather than as representative of healthcare professionals in oncological surgery as a whole.
ncb039f794dc6: Background An efficient referral system is an important but often under-recognized determinant of survival in critically ill children. Previous studies have reported high mortality rates among pediatric patients transferred to tertiary care facilities. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-level referral hospital in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Material and methods This prospective cohort study was conducted over a 12-month period (July 1, 2023, to June 30, 2024) and included all critically ill children admitted to the PICU following interhospital referral. Demographic, clinical, referral, and transport data were prospectively collected. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PICU mortality. Results A total of 334 children were included, with a median age of 6 years. PICU mortality was 25.4%. The most common referral indication based on the Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was central nervous system dysfunction. Pre-referral management most commonly included oxygen therapy, antibiotic administration, and fluid resuscitation. Compared with survivors, non-survivors had higher PELOD-2 scores and were more likely to require intubation, mechanical ventilation, and vasoactive support before referral. In the multivariable analysis, pre-referral vasoactive support (adjusted OR 2.23, 95% CI 1.20–4.15; P = 0.011) and higher PELOD-2 scores within the first 24 hours after PICU admission (adjusted OR 1.32 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 1.20–1.45; P < 0.001) were independently associated with PICU mortality. Referral distance, decision time, and transfer time were not independently associated with mortality. Conclusion PICU mortality among critically ill children transferred and admitted to a tertiary-care hospital in Indonesia remains high. Pre-referral vasoactive support and higher PELOD-2 scores at PICU admission were independently associated with PICU mortality. These findings generate the hypothesis that improvements in early stabilization and communication may improve outcomes, warranting prospective evaluation.
n197e63840e22: The injection molding of bridge-type compliant mechanisms is sensitive to non-uniform mold temperature because the thin flexure hinges are prone to premature solidification and incomplete filling. This study evaluates a fluid-layer-assisted mold temperature-control architecture using experimental thermography, transient thermo-fluid simulation, a representative straight-channel thermal baseline, melt-filling analysis, and displacement testing of molded HDPE mechanisms. The fluid-layer thermo-fluid model was validated against infrared measurements, yielding a mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.01 °C and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 6.44 °C across six validation points. Under the numerical benchmark condition of an 80 °C inlet temperature, a mass flow rate of 59.5 g/s, and 40 s heating, the fluid-layer architecture was predicted to increase the average cavity-surface temperature by approximately 4.0 °C and reduce the maximum longitudinal temperature difference by 28.6% relative to the straight-channel model. Independent thermography of a representative steel straight-channel insert under the same inlet-temperature and flow-rate conditions showed a lower and more non-uniform surface-temperature field than the steel fluid-layer configuration, confirming the direction of the predicted thermal advantage. Melt-filling simulations subsequently predicted incomplete filling at the thin flexure region for the straight-channel configuration and complete filling for the fluid-layer configuration; this filling comparison remains simulation-based. For HDPE blends containing 0–25 wt% recycled material, the molded mechanisms retained an approximately linear input–output displacement response over the investigated range. At an input displacement of approximately 175 µm, the mean output displacement decreased from 857 µm for virgin HDPE to 745 µm at 25 wt% recycled HDPE. The results support the fluid-layer architecture as a conventionally machinable approach for improving mold-surface thermal control, while polymer morphology, fatigue durability, and experimental straight-channel filling remain subjects for future work.
n95c95a0c7e70: This study examines how organisational and technological antecedents shape management accounting information quality and adoption level among Vietnamese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and how these characteristics influence decision quality and business performance, with business environment uncertainty as a moderator. Using a cross-sectional survey of 503 Vietnamese SME managers, the study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and importance-performance map analysis to test a five-antecedent serial mediation model grounded in contingency theory and information processing theory. All ten hypotheses were supported. Information technology capability was the strongest driver of accounting information quality (β = 0.508), and market competition intensity was the strongest driver of adoption level (β = 0.385). Decision quality was the strongest direct driver of business performance (β = 0.558), and business environment uncertainty positively moderated this relationship (β = 0.238). All five serial indirect paths to business performance were statistically significant. The importance-performance analysis identified information technology capability as the highest-priority investment area, combining high importance with low realised performance (52.01 out of 100). To our knowledge, this study offers one of the first comprehensive tests of a serial mediation model linking these antecedents to business performance through accounting characteristics and decision quality in Vietnamese SMEs, one of the first importance-performance prioritisation maps for managers in this context, and extends contingency theory by identifying business environment uncertainty as a pure moderator rather than a direct antecedent. Findings suggest Vietnamese SME managers should prioritise digital accounting infrastructure investment ahead of expanding accounting tool adoption, and that government support for digital accounting tools may be warranted. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, partly addressed through theoretically grounded antecedent ordering, predictive validity testing, and multi-method bias assessment; the single-country scope reflects Vietnam's structural representativeness of wider ASEAN transition economies.
n70d70d4ba088: Digital media can increase the visibility of living heritage without securing understanding or sustained engagement. We examined how public digital discourse about the Twenty-Four Solar Terms can be translated into an interpretive stimulus and how users evaluate it. We collected 3,433 publicly visible online text units and retained 1,101 after cleaning and anonymisation. The retained corpus informed collaborative thematic reading; 1,089 texts met the token threshold for keyword extraction and auxiliary topic-model inspection. Thematic analysis identified six cultural theme categories. They covered seasonal diet and bodily care; temporal order and heritage knowledge; and natural phenology and seasonal perception. They also covered folk customs and ritual life; aesthetic imagery and digital creative expression; and agricultural production and everyday practice. These categories informed a five-page storyboard through theme-design mapping and expert-assisted review. Survey data from 350 valid respondents were analysed with covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) and supplementary fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Information clarity, visual aesthetics, perceived explorability and perceived authenticity were positively associated with perceived cultural value. Perceived explorability had the largest standardised path estimate for cultural value, and perceived authenticity was also associated with cultural identity. Perceived cultural value and cultural identity were associated with sustained cultural engagement intention. Configurational analysis identified four sufficient configurations for high engagement and four for low engagement. The two solution sets were asymmetric rather than mirror images. These findings link perceived interpretive qualities, cultural value and cultural identity with sustained cultural engagement intention.
nef42fa318b37: The autonomic nervous system regulates cardiovascular homeostasis during stressors such as heat, but the effects of type 2 diabetes (T2D) with hypertension on such responses are unclear. Twenty male participants (10 with type 2 diabetes and hypertension and 10 age-matched healthy controls; mean ages 64 ± 4.14 and 63 ± 5.42 years) underwent a 90-minute whole-body heat exposure at 40 °C and 50% relative humidity. Heart rate variability (HRV), baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), and blood pressure variability (BPV) were assessed before, during and after the heat exposure. Heat exposure increased heart rate in both groups but this response was less in T2D (5.43 bpm; ~ 7% increase) versus controls (13.96 bpm; ~ 22% increase; p = 0.014). Similarly, reductions in HRV indices to heat stress were generally smaller in magnitude among participants with T2D. For example, high-frequency power (HF RR) decreased by 31.21 ms² (~54.5% reduction) in T2D because of heat exposure, compared with a reduction of 179.35 ms² (~74% reduction) in controls (p = 0.038). Further, LF BRS decreased by 1.07 ms/mmHg (~25% reduction) vs. 3.96 ms/mmHg (~51% reduction) (p = 0.021), HF BRS by 1.58 ms/mmHg (~35% reduction) vs. 4.15 ms/mmHg (~62% reduction) (p = 0.034), and mean BRS by 1.18 ms/mmHg (~26% reduction) vs. 4.16 ms/mmHg (~58% reduction) (p = 0.010) in those with T2D versus controls, respectively. Low-frequency power (LF RR), LF/HF ratio and BPV parameters also showed smaller (though nonsignificant) changes in T2D. Overall, combined T2D and hypertension produced blunted autonomic responses to short-term heat exposure, potentially increasing vulnerability to temperature extremes.
n30b10dc3afc5: Mutations of EIF2AK4, which encodes the eIF2α kinase GCN2, cause a severe inherited form of pulmonary hypertension called pulmonary veno-occlusive disease (PVOD). Some pathogenic variants of GCN2 are amenable to pharmacological reactivation by low concentrations of ATP pocket-binding inhibitors. Kinase inhibition at modestly elevated concentrations limits the clinical utility of these drugs against PVOD. We therefore performed an in cellulo chemical screen for GCN2 activators and identified three structurally distinct compounds with low micromolar stimulatory activities. Unlike previously described GCN2 activators, one of these molecules activated GCN2 independently of GCN1. Modelling supported by structure activity screens suggested it binds within the ATP pocket of GCN2, but unlike existing ligands does not protrude inward into the allosteric pocket or outward into the solvent. This overcomes a key requirement of other GCN2 activators.
n33e898a8ad96: Two types of osteoblasts are required to assemble the zebrafish embryonic skeleton: classical osteoblasts homologous to the mammalian cell and notochord sheath cells which serve as non-classical osteoblasts. The gene entpd5a is critically required for ossification via both types of osteoblasts. Despite the indispensability of zebrafish models in vertebrate research, the genetic regulation of bone formation, as well as mechanisms of transcriptional control of entpd5a, remains largely unknown. Here, using a newly generated transgenic line, we isolate classical and non-classical osteoblasts from zebrafish embryos and performed both assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC)-seq and RNA-seq. We analysed results independently and integratively to understand those chromatin dynamics and accompanying transcriptomic changes that occur in different skeletal cell types. We show that although Dlx family factors are playing important roles in classical osteoblast regulation, Hox family factors are involved in governing spinal ossification via non-classical osteoblasts. We further present a resource-driven analysis of the entpd5a promoter, experimentally validating the ATAC-seq dataset and proposing mechanisms of regulating the complex entpd5a expression pattern during zebrafish osteogenesis. Our results thus provide a necessary comprehensive resource for the field of bone development and indicate spatio-temporally regulated promoter/enhancer interactions taking place in the entpd5a locus.
nfb8960c5450b: The most widespread animal life cycle includes a planktonic larval stage that is environmentally induced to settle and rapidly metamorphose into a benthic juvenile. Although this transition is critical for survival, how planetary cues such as light interact with local ecological signals to prepare the genome for such rapid reprogramming remains poorly understood. Here, using the sponge Amphimedon queenslandica, we integrate time-resolved transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling across larval competence, settlement, and the first hours of metamorphosis. We show that diminishing light at sunset is associated with extensive chromatin remodelling in swimming larvae prior to settlement despite relatively modest changes in gene expression. Upon environmental induction by a coralline alga, metamorphosis is accompanied by the rapid and transient activation of a large suite of deeply conserved transcription factors (TFs), including AP-1/bZIP family members, whose binding motifs are enriched in newly accessible regulatory regions near differentially expressed genes. Larvae prevented from experiencing sunset by constant light fail to settle and instead adopt an alternative transcriptional and chromatin state characterised by widespread loss of accessibility and repression of competence-associated TFs, including the circadian regulator CLOCK and other bHLH-PAS factors. These observations support a model in which light-entrained transcriptional activity establishes an anticipatory, permissive chromatin landscape that enables immediate and coordinated transcriptional reprogramming upon environmental induction. We propose that such chromatin priming may represent a broadly deployed regulatory strategy underlying the speed and robustness of metamorphosis in biphasic animal life cycles.
ne937d3f2afc6: Mosquito-borne virus transmission is increasing globally. Due to a lack of effective vaccines or targeted treatments, mitigation relies on reducing human exposure to infectious mosquitoes. Entomological surveillance provides estimates of human risk by quantifying the prevalence of arboviruses in mosquito populations. Testing of pooled mosquitoes via RT-qPCR is often used to infer infection prevalence; however, these data are often binarised and ignore semi-quantitative cycle threshold (Ct values) that may provide valuable information on virus kinetics, mosquito infectiousness, and ultimately human risk. West Nile virus (WNV) is a globally distributed arbovirus and endemic to the United States. In this study, we analysed pooled Ct values from retrospective mosquito surveillance and found substantial variation that could not be explained by laboratory factors alone. To understand how underlying viral load and epidemiological dynamics might explain this variation, we developed a multi-scale model linking pooled Ct values to heterogeneous within-host viral kinetics in mosquitoes and birds and seasonal transmission dynamics. Our modelling suggests that Ct values from positive pools might reflect a mixture of potentially infectious and non-infectious mosquitoes, indicating that a substantial proportion of PCR-positive mosquitoes might not contribute to transmission. We then developed a method to estimate mosquito infection prevalence using only pooled Ct values that distinguishes infectious from non-infectious prevalence. Estimates of overall prevalence were comparable to standard methods using binarised data and remained accurate at higher prevalences where standard approaches fail. Overall, these findings demonstrate that entomological viral load data reflect biologically meaningful variation in mosquito infection status that is lost through binarisation. Accounting for heterogeneous mosquito viral kinetics can improve interpretation of surveillance data and estimates of transmission risk, with implications for arbovirus surveillance beyond WNV.
na9b5be8accd9: The brain is one of the most complex animal organs, and the development of the many different neuron types remains enigmatic. A set of brain-specific transcription factors is involved in brain patterning, but their specific contributions mostly remain to be elucidated, including foxQ2II. This transcription factor is conserved in anterior neuroectodermal patterning of most animals, while it has been lost from vertebrates. The contribution of foxQ2II-positive neurons to the adult brain has remained enigmatic. Here, we use our enhancer trap, immunostainings, and our newly established beetle brainbow system to categorize Tc-foxQ2II-positive neurons into nine clusters with different projection patterns. All clusters contain neurons with the fast-activating neurotransmitters acetylcholine and glutamate, while no Tc-foxQ2II-positive neuron is GABA-ergic or serotonin-positive. Interestingly, we found that many dopaminergic neurons were Tc-foxQ2II positive and homologize them with dopaminergic neurons of the PPL2c, PPM1, and PPL1 cluster described in the Drosophila brain. Our results show that Tc-foxQ2II marks subsets of fast-acting interneurons contributing to the higher-order brain centers mushroom bodies and central complex. Taken together, our work expands the known functional range of foxQ2 genes from sensory and neurosecretory cell specification to interneurons involved in the function of higher-order brain centers.
nb45012d98ac2: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. Using a common garden experiment with 110 genotypes of the cosmopolitan grass Phragmites australis, we first established that the imposed salinity treatment induced strong multilevel stress responses: above-ground biomass declined by >60%, sodium accumulated three- to fivefold across all leaf stages, and 484 metabolites showed significant differential accumulation, including canonical markers of osmotic and oxidative stress. Against this backdrop of confirmed stress, we found that nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE) remained largely unaffected by salinity. Instead, NuRE was strongly correlated with phylogeographic lineage, ecotype, and latitude of origin, demonstrating evolutionary canalization rather than short-term acclimation. Element-specific regulatory patterns were also evident: while phosphorus resorption followed concentration-dependent control regardless of stress, nitrogen control was disrupted under salinity, and potassium resorption showed no such dependence. Our findings reveal that intraspecific variation in nutrient resorption is predominantly shaped by historical adaptation and geographic context, not by plasticity to salinity. This genetic canalization of a key functional trait implies that predictions of nutrient cycling under global change must account for the phylogeographic composition of plant populations.
n3e98ebe5bbd3: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.
n5f1052fbb9df: Visualizing the structures of small proteins and complexes has been a longstanding challenge in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Some of these targets have been successfully resolved by binding to antibody fragments (Fabs) or fusing with external scaffolds to increase their size. Recent advances in conventional single-particle techniques have enabled the determination of an increasing number of structures smaller than 100 kDa, achieving resolutions relevant to drug research. Compared to X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM preserves the near-native states of biomolecules, can resolve structural heterogeneity, and has the potential to apply to a wide range of targets. In this work, we demonstrate that the alignment and reconstruction of small macromolecular complexes can be improved using high-resolution structures as priors, combined with 2D template matching. Using this method, we reconstructed a previously intractable ∼43 kDa protein kinase and improved the density of its ligand-binding site. Our theoretical analysis predicts that this method can further extend single-particle cryo-EM to important drug-binding complexes well below 50 kDa.
n34636b57b955: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run with immunohistochemistry and functional studies, we found that the Atf4-Chop axis suppresses proliferation via the cell-cycle inhibitor Btg2. Together, our findings support a model in which mid-zone hepatocytes transiently prioritize stress adaptation over proliferation, thereby preserving regenerative capacity for subsequent liver repair.
n67157421fd0e: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.
n7addc66065b1: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is a key antiviral target that equilibrates between an active dimer and inactive monomer, making the dimerization interface a promising therapeutic vulnerability. This study investigates Mpro monomer-dimer equilibrium and conformational changes induced by inhibitor binding using 13C labeling with native mass spectrometry and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). We evaluated how peptidomimetic inhibitors (PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, boceprevir) and non-peptidomimetic inhibitors (carmofur, ebselen, MR6-31-2, AT7519, pelitinib) influence Mpro dimerization and subunit exchange. Key findings revealed divergent mechanisms: peptidomimetic inhibitors significantly shifted the equilibrium towards the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange dynamics and rigidifying the dimer interface; in contrast, ebselen impaired dimer formation and increased interface flexibility. Notably, tandem mass spectrometry identified a novel covalent binding site for ebselen at C300. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses demonstrated that this C300 modification allosterically alters the hydrogen bond network of the dimer interface, directly contributing to ebselen-mediated dimer disruption and enzymatic inhibition. Overall, this study clarifies distinct inhibitory modes between peptidomimetics and ebselen, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting allosteric sites at the dimer interface for designing next-generation Mpro inhibitors.
n6c8eb0508434: The evolutionary arms race between plants and insects involves not only direct defense and counter-defense but also sophisticated resource manipulation. However, how herbivorous insects respond to host nutritional signals to modulate their fitness traits remains unclear. This study investigates how the small brown planthopper (SBPH, Laodelphax striatellus) manipulates host plant carbohydrate allocation, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the acquired glucose enhances SBPH fecundity and insecticide tolerance. Using molecular, pharmacological, and biochemical approaches, we found that SBPH infestation induced systemic carbohydrate reallocation in rice, elevating whole-plant glucose levels by promoting aerial accumulation while depleting root reserves. Host-derived glucose enhanced SBPH fecundity by activating the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, upregulating juvenile hormone (JH) signaling, and increasing vitellogenin production. For imidacloprid tolerance, glucose boosted glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity via two synergistic mechanisms: by upregulating glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to increase glutathione synthesis, and transcriptionally via the glucose-TOR-JH axis to induce LsGSTe1 (SBPH epsilon class GST) and LsGSTo1 (SBPH omega class GST) expression. Our findings establish host-derived glucose as a central signaling molecule that SBPH utilizes to modulate conserved pathways for simultaneous optimization of reproduction and insecticide resistance. This reveals a multifaceted nutrient-responsive mechanism in insect pests and identifies the glucose-TOR-JH axis as critical molecular targets for developing nutrient-based pest control strategies, such as disrupting insect nutrient-sensing pathways or modulating host carbohydrate metabolism.
n2d3bfbd3d4b4: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH (https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/, https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.
n88df928e4c65: Quantum geometry plays a fundamental role in many aspects of condensed matter physics. Among its central objects are the Berry curvature and the quantum metric—quantities that, while distinct, are intertwined through geometric constraints. In this article, we survey recent progress in understanding when and how this bound is saturated, with particular emphasis on the emergence of momentum-space holomorphicity of Bloch states. These developments highlight a profound connection between certain ideal Bloch bands and the Hilbert space structure of the lowest Landau level. We elucidate this relationship through a review of quantum Hall physics in both homogeneous and spatially varying magnetic fields and conclude by exploring its implications for the search for fractionalized phases in emerging platforms, including moiré materials.
n9a95df70102a: This article is a gentle stroll through the field of optimization and optimal control, aiming to acquaint the reader with the evolution of developments leading up to the Pontryagin maximum principle. The exposition adheres to simplicity without sacrificing integrity. The continuous versions of results are derived as limits of discrete versions, thus adopting a unified approach to finite-dimensional and function spaces, and wherever permissible, an intuitive connection to physics is established. Complete proofs are not provided; instead, the key geometric ideas in the proofs are presented.
n655877e57217: Invasive exotic arthropods and weeds pose a growing threat to biodiversity, food security, and the functioning of whole ecosystems, resulting in significant socioeconomic and ecological impacts. Classical biological control—the importation of specialist natural enemies from the native range—can lead to long-term, sustainable pest suppression, but it is typically implemented reactively after the invasive species is established and is causing significant negative impacts. Proactive biological control offers an anticipatory approach, developing biological control agents before or shortly after establishment and enabling rapid response to new incursions. This review examines current applications, opportunities, and challenges of proactive strategies and proposes steps to advance proactive management of invasive arthropod pests and weeds.
nfd78a74cc8d9: T cell receptor–engineered T (TCR-T) cell therapy has emerged as a promising adoptive cellular therapy for solid tumors by enabling recognition of intracellular antigens presented via human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules. Unlike chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy, TCR-T cell therapy targets a broader antigen repertoire, including cancer-testis antigens, neoantigens, and viral antigens. Recent clinical advances, highlighted by the approval of afamitresgene autoleucel in synovial sarcoma, demonstrate meaningful antitumor activity. However, several limitations remain, including HLA restriction, antigen heterogeneity, toxicity related to on-target/off-tumor effects, and mechanisms of resistance such as antigen loss and T cell exhaustion. Advances in antigen selection, gene editing, and synthetic biology are improving both safety and efficacy. Combination strategies and next-generation engineered constructs are expected to overcome current barriers. This review summarizes the biological rationale, clinical evidence, safety considerations, and resistance mechanisms of TCR-T cell therapy in solid tumors and discusses future directions to optimize their therapeutic potential.
n789e4ad2e301: Bacteria use membraneless compartments, or biomolecular condensates, to organize cellular processes in space and time. These condensates assemble and function within a highly constrained physical landscape shaped by a crowded cytoplasm, structured nucleoid, membrane surfaces, and distinct polar zones. In this review, we examine condensates involved in genome maintenance, RNA metabolism, cell division, signaling, and metabolic regulation, focusing on how cellular microenvironments and physiological state shape when and where these condensates form, which molecules they recruit, and the material states they adopt. In turn, condensates can concentrate molecules for biochemical reactions, sequester them for storage or protection, release or redistribute them as conditions change, and position them at specific cellular sites. Disentangling the contribution of the condensed state from that of the underlying molecular interactions will be essential for determining how condensates regulate bacterial physiology.
nbe59f49b00ea: Eppur si muove —the work of Galileo Galilei marked the beginning of the quantitative study of motion for scope-observable entities. Extending this physics-based perspective to the microscope-observable microbial world has uncovered principles of motion that diverge sharply from our everyday intuition, revealing physics as being essential to understanding microbial motility. In this review, we explore the fundamental physical principles that enable and constrain the motility strategies evolved by diverse microorganisms, with a focus on prokaryotes, to enable propulsion in fluids and along surfaces. We examine how microbial motility functions in complex, heterogeneous environments, and we provide a brief evolutionary perspective on microbial motility by highlighting its costs and benefits. In summary, we show how including a physical approach in the study of microbial motility both unveils general solutions and specific adaptations and enables a better understanding of a world for which our intuition is not trained.
n0147da51a5b2: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.
n01db1bbde499: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common in natural environments, including the microbiota of animal and human hosts. The local physical, chemical, and biological conditions of environmental patches and matrices vary both qualitatively and quantitatively. Often, these conditions are found as gradients, creating intersections that can either facilitate or inhibit the spread and evolution of antibiotic resistance (AbR). Ecological kinetics (EcoK) describes how combinations of these conditions influence the abundance and transmission of antibiotic-resistant populations, as well as the mobile genetic elements that carry resistance genes. Evolutionary dynamics (EvoD) concerns the effects of environmental conditions on genetic variation, the expression of resistance traits, and the evolvability of host bacteria, ultimately contributing to the emergence and selection of AbR. This review examines the influence of numerous environmental conditions on EcoK and EvoD. This field remains poorly understood, and further research is essential to identify high-risk areas where surveillance for the emergence and spread of AbR should be implemented.
n0c668217e858: In all living cells, chemical reactions known as metabolism generate energy and building blocks for cellular structures. Metabolism produces and consumes ATP, the major currency of cellular energy. Because approximately 85% of ATP is bound to Mg 2+ , bacteria reduce their ATP concentration when cytoplasmic Mg 2+ availability drops below a certain threshold. This reduction in ATP concentration reshapes metabolism and gene transcription as well as protein synthesis, solubility, and turnover. This article reviews how ATP acts both directly and via ATP-derived signaling molecules, such as 3′,5′-cyclic AMP (cAMP), bis-(3′,5′)-cyclic dimeric-AMP (c-di-AMP), diadenosine tetraphosphate (Ap 4 A), and guanosine-3′,5′-tetra- and pentaphosphate [(p)ppGpp], which direct adaptations to stresses bacteria experience in their natural environments. It also discusses how Mg 2+ -responsive regulatory systems supersede canonical control of metabolism and protein homeostasis by governing ATP amounts and how this bacterial response slows growth, modifies cell envelope structures, and favors survival.
n6bce9b30997a: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based therapies marked a major breakthrough in obesity pharmacotherapy, while subsequent advancements targeting multiple entero-pancreatic hormones now deliver weight loss previously achievable only with bariatric surgery, alongside improvements in obesity-related complications. Despite this progress, significant challenges persist, including reduced efficacy in diabetic populations, gastrointestinal adverse effects, and high costs that drive a real-world adherence gap. Consequently, next-generation therapies, including receptor polyagonists, oral formulations, and small-molecule incretin mimetics with optimized pharmacokinetic profiles, are being developed to enhance efficacy, tolerability, and accessibility while maintaining safety. However, weight regain after treatment cessation remains a critical hurdle. Growing evidence underscores the importance of sustained lifestyle interventions and muscle mass preservation to facilitate weight stabilization. Concurrently, research is heavily focused on identifying the biological drivers of weight regain, such as altered neuroregulation, metabolic adaptation, and adipose tissue remodeling. This review examines the current landscape, limitations, and emerging strategies of obesity pharmacotherapy.

n1244691a4e1e: Interleukin-21 receptor engagement initiates a Janus kinase–signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signalling cascade that activates several STAT proteins that drive the germinal centre (GC) response. However, the relative effects of IL-21 on individual STAT proteins during the differentiation of T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and GC B cells has been difficult to distinguish. Here, we characterize a novel mutation in the interleukin-21 receptor (IL-21REINS) that creates a dominant defect in the activation of STAT1. Our findings provide evidence that IL-21-mediated activation of STAT1 has a non-redundant role in the differentiation of Tfh cells following T-dependent immunization. IL-21REINS Tfh cells were even more impaired than Tfh cells genetically deficient in IL-21R, questioning our current understanding of the role of IL-21 derived from protein knockout mice. The observation that functional compensation fails in the presence of the IL-21R hypomorph provides insight into how underlying compensation can impact our interpretation of a complex biological system.
nd029882b919f: Large language models based on the transformer architecture are now capable of producing human-like language. But do they encode and process linguistic meaning in a human-like way? Here, we address this question by analysing 7T fMRI data from 30 participants reading 108 sentences each. These sentences are carefully designed to disentangle sentence structure from word meaning, thereby testing whether transformer representations of sentence meaning resemble those formed by the brain. Using representational similarity analysis, we compared representations from eight transformers and eleven other semantic models to brain activity in language regions of interest. We found that while transformer models match brain representations better than models that completely ignore word order, all transformers poorly match human brain representations of sentences that require sensitivity to structural relations such as semantic roles (who did what to whom). Further, transformers were significantly inferior to models explicitly designed to encode the structural relations between words. Our results provide insight into the nature of sentence representation in the brain, highlighting the critical role of sentence structure. They also cast doubt on the claim that transformers represent sentence meaning similarly to the human brain.
nf4f0b11fa06c: The zona incerta (ZI) is a deep brain region originally described by Auguste Forel as an ‘immensely confusing area about which nothing can be said’. Despite the elusive nature of this structure, mounting evidence supports the role of the ZI and surrounding regions across a diverse range of brain functions and as a candidate target for neuromodulatory therapies. Using in vivo diffusion magnetic resonance imaging and data-driven connectivity, we identify a topographic organization between the ZI and neocortex. Specifically, our methods identify a rostral–caudal gradient predominantly connecting the frontopolar and ventral prefrontal cortices with the rostral ZI, and the primary sensorimotor cortices with the caudal ZI. Moreover, we demonstrate how clustering and gradient approaches build complementary evidence including facilitating the mapping of a central region of the ZI, connected with the dorsal prefrontal cortex. These results were shown to be replicable across multiple datasets and at the individual subject level, building evidence for the important role of the ZI in mediating frontal lobe-associated tasks, ranging from motor to cognitive to emotional control. Finally, we consider the impact of this topographic organization on the refinement of neuromodulatory targets. These results pave the way for an increasingly detailed understanding of ZI substructures, and considerations for in vivo targeting of the ZI for neuromodulation.
na3412ebfff91: Nav1.7 voltage-gated sodium channels are strongly expressed in human primary pain-sensing neurons (nociceptors), and selective Nav1.7 inhibitors have been developed as possible therapeutic agents for treating pain, so far with disappointing clinical results. In contrast, a selective Nav1.8 channel inhibitor (suzetrigine) has had successful clinical trials. Because nociceptors express both Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 channels, it is of interest to compare effects of Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 inhibitors on the excitability of human nociceptors. To compare with previous results with suzetrigine, we characterized the effects of a selective Nav1.7 inhibitor, AM-2099, on action potential generation and repetitive firing of dissociated human dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, studied at 37°C. Inhibition of Nav1.7 channels by 600 nM AM-2099 generally produced a substantial depolarizing shift of action potential threshold, an increase in rheobase, a decrease in action potential upstroke velocity, decrease in action potential peak, and prolongation of the refractory period. Compared to inhibition of Nav1.8 channels, inhibition of Nav1.7 channels had larger effects on threshold and maximal upstroke velocity, while action potential peak was reduced similarly by both. Nav1.8 inhibition produced much more dramatic reduction of repetitive firing than Nav1.7 inhibition. The results show that although the excitability of human DRG neurons is affected by inhibition of Nav1.7 channels, most notably by an increase in threshold and increase in refractory period, repetitive firing of the neurons in response to strong stimuli is little affected.
nae30eedf1261: This study provides a comprehensive ultrastructural analysis of the pharyngeal sensory system in Drosophila melanogaster larvae, focusing on the four major pharyngeal sense organs: the ventral pharyngeal sensilla (VPS), dorsal pharyngeal sensilla (DPS), dorsal pharyngeal organ (DPO), and posterior pharyngeal sensilla (PPS). Our analysis revealed 15 sensilla across these organs, comprising four mechanosensory, nine chemosensory, and two dual-function sensilla. We identified 35 Type I neurons (6 mechanosensory and 29 chemosensory) and 6 Type II neurons with putative chemosensory functions. Additional sensory structures, including papilla sensilla and chordotonal organs in the cephalopharyngeal region, were characterized. This detailed mapping and classification of pharyngeal sensory structures completes their structural characterization and provides a foundation for future anatomical and functional studies of sensory perception in insects. This work represents a significant step toward a complete analysis of the larval sensory system, providing new opportunities for investigating how an organism processes sensory information to navigate and interact with its environment.
n0ab99943e7ed: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) causes more deaths annually than any other pathogen, yet an effective vaccine remains elusive. IFN-γ-producing Th1 CD4+ T cells are necessary but insufficient for protection against infection. In humans, the development of IL-17A-producing Th17 T cells correlates with protection; however, not all individuals develop a Th17 response. In mice, experimental vaccines can elicit protective Th17 cells, yet Th17s are rare in primary infection. Why Mtb fails to consistently elicit Th17s is unknown. n089630dc6e4b: Women have long been underrepresented in biomedical research, prompting efforts to make research more sex inclusive. ncea4acd33b2d: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.
n7f3c4ea9b936: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. n601bcd0527b0: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. Motor units, each of which consists of a single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates, contribute to the total activation of each muscle through their recruitment and firing rate when active. However, it remains unknown how the nervous system controls locomotor speed by changing the firing of individual motor units. To address this, we combined quantitative behavioral analysis of mouse locomotion with single motor unit recordings from the lateral and long heads of the triceps brachii, which drive monoarticular extension of the elbow and biarticular movements of the elbow and shoulder, respectively. In contrast to prior studies employing bulk electromyography (EMG) to examine muscle activity, our recordings revealed the diversity of spike patterning across motor units, as well as systematic differences in motor unit activity across muscles and locomotor speeds. First, motor unit activity differed significantly across the lateral and long heads, suggesting differential control of these two closely apposed elbow extensor muscles. Second, we found that individual units were recruited probabilistically (during only a subset of strides), showing that the highly repeatable bulk EMG signals observed across strides, in fact, reflect varying subsets of individual motor units. Finally, although recruitment probability and firing rate both increased at faster walking speeds, increases in recruitment were proportionally larger than rate changes, and recruitment of individual units accompanied changes in limb kinematics. Together, these results reveal how the firing of individual motor units varies systematically across muscles and walking speeds to produce flexible locomotor behavior.
n52da83b80ad0: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. We show that the odorant 1-octanol is encoded combinatorially in the periphery as both an attractant and a repellent. These inputs are integrated centrally, and their relative strengths determine the sensitivity and valence of the behavioral response through modulation of locomotory reversals and speed. The balance of these pathways also dictates the activity of the locomotory command interneurons, which control locomotory reversals. This balance serves as a regulatory node for response modulation, allowing C. elegans to weigh opportunities and hazards in its environment when formulating behavioral responses. Thus, an odorant can be encoded simultaneously as inputs of opposite valence, focusing attention on the integration of these inputs in determining perception, response, and plasticity.
n6808a24d9bca: As elsewhere in the world, archaeological records in eastern Africa show that long environmental variabilities shaped the emergence and development of farming economies. Marine sediments and isotopic data indicate alternating humid and arid phases that coincide with the reorganization of settlements, establishment of agricultural landscapes, and the generation of new subsistence practices during the later Holocene. Strengthened monsoons during the African Humid Period (13,050–3050 BCE) produced environments that enabled human mobility, likely experimentation with plants, and the dispersal of early herders through the Rift Valley and the Horn of Africa. Archaeological, archaeobotanical, isotopic, and other data from sites in the Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, and elsewhere indicate varied and gradual transitions from foraging to mixed farming, shaped by microenvironments, altitude, and intercommunity exchanges. Case studies of farming systems developed over the last 2,000 years demonstrate innovative forms of resilient landscape engineering and complex social management. We suggest that the equity and collective stewardship attested by this record offer valuable analogues for contemporary climate adaptation in the Anthropocene.
n1ac9129e894b: This reflection on my years in linguistic anthropology also includes the broader sociohistorical transformations of which I have been a part. The Cold War and its aftermath were the backdrop against which we learned and taught. As a child migrant to the United States from the Soviet region, I became fascinated by the intersection of political relationships and linguistic practices. At the same time, linguistic anthropology was starting to navigate between theories of political economy and the analysis of speaking as action-in-events. Within that endeavor, I have studied conceptual questions about multilingualism and the workings of language ideology as well as questions about sign phenomena in constructing gender, sociocultural differentiation, scaling, and translation. My scholarly path has depended on the generous, inspiring influence of mentors, colleagues, and students, individually and in the many seminars and study groups we have formed together. Working now on analyzing authoritarian regimes, I see with alarm their effects on public expression, safety, and protest, echoing my earliest memories of repression.
nc37ea52f64d4: How anthropologists have invoked and conceptualized anxiety reflects the development of new ways of relating selfhood, subjectivity, and the sociopolitical to each other. This article examines the recent development of anthropological frameworks of anxiety in the context of the rising prevalence of and interest in anxiety. Since its inception in modern social theory, anxiety has functioned as a commentary on people's relation to risk, precarity, and emerging forms of capitalism. Early anthropological approaches to anxiety relied extensively on psychological theories that focused on the emotions at an individual level. Although they framed anxiety as a social condition in addition to an inner one, they were still beholden to the politics and ethics of the sovereign subject and dichotomies between self and society, individual and collective, and citizen and state. By framing anxiety as a social practice and relation, contemporary anthropologists are now redefining anxiety's role in political-economic transformations from a passive reflection of widespread uncertainty and insecurity to an agentive constituent of politics itself.
nb7d681096d2b: A review of the anthropological literature motivates an expansive definition of the therapeutic as practices that have or are purported to have salubrious effects on at least one of the parties involved. Those effects could be on the psychic or spiritual state of participants (i.e., what one is or has), on how they make sense of their state or circumstances (i.e., how one sees, feels, understands, or knows), and/or on their behavior (i.e., what one does and says, how, and to what effect). The idea that the therapeutic is invariably a matter of communicative practice is a premise of this review, which addresses ( a ) the diversity and distinctiveness of therapies as multimodal genres; ( b ) the therapeutic distillation of cultural values, projects, and ideals; ( c ) the epistemic and interpretive challenges of therapeutic communication, particularly relative to politically loaded questions of mediation; and ( d ) the scaling of the therapeutic as a kind of communication by way of communication.
n86ff13de8d4a: This article provides an overview of experimental anthropology, arguing that, from its inception, anthropology has operated as a form of experimental inquiry aimed at producing a surplus of data, relations, and sensations. We explore this notion through a tripartite heuristic for understanding how anthropological creativity draws on methods from the natural sciences as well as from art and design: ( a ) experience-based experimentation, ( b ) the adoption of scientific protocols and instruments, and ( c ) experimentation with and through models. Despite the apparent diversity of contemporary approaches, efforts to reimagine experimentalism in anthropology can still be understood through this heuristic. We revisit it in reverse order, arguing, first, that modeling now takes place through prototypes, games, devices, and other relational infrastructures; second, that apparatus-based experimentation has opened new possibilities for sensory enrichment; and finally, that anthropological practice itself emerges as a radical venture that expands conceptual, physical, and existential boundaries, with ethnographic inquiry relentlessly generating excess data.
n727fc55c624a: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.
ncfa127a7cc72: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.
n263ea53659a4: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.
nddc746c4812f: Candida ( Candidozyma ) auris is a pathogenic fungus first identified in a patient in 2009. The C. auris clades mostly diverged from one another 5,000–10,000 years ago, during a period when global temperatures and sea levels rose and coastal wetlands flourished. Within the past 200–300 years, a new wave of rapid divergence occurred within each clade. This corresponds to industrialization, urbanization, global warming, and the widespread wetland destruction. Environmental stressors, including heat, are hypothesized to have driven mutations and stress resistance. These may not only help C. auris withstand a changing climate but also help it thrive within mammalian hosts.
nc2e699c45070: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is caused by CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 , leading to gene silencing and loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP). n4e194ecc00f6: Dinosaurs dominated terrestrial ecosystems for more than 160 million years under fluctuating atmospheric conditions that profoundly shaped their cardiovascular physiology. This review synthesizes current knowledge on sauropods cardiovascular physiology, focusing on cardiac function, vascular architecture, O 2 transport, and whole-organism integration.
ne2e3bf4ba4c6: Cellular senescence is a stress-responsive cell fate characterized by stable growth arrest and acquisition of a proinflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype. n4a7543508958: The capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. n4e9b434f9b80: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. n4993b2be88a7: Understanding the taxonomic affinity of putative avialan teeth is essential to assessing the geographic range and richness of Late Cretaceous toothed birds. n760d688f9262: Hybrid quantum–classical machine learning on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices suffers from three coupled overheads: hardware miscalibration, classical syndrome-decoding latency and shot noise on gradient estimators. Three theoretical bounds characterize the joint effect on logical error rate (LER), convergence rate and observable variance. On device-calibrated noise-model simulators (n=20 seeds), QCOP achieves up to 2× wall-clock training speed-up and approximately 40% variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) energy error reduction relative to the unaugmented baseline. A hardware pilot on ibm_nairobi at surface-code distance d=5 (2000 syndrome volumes, 8192 shots each, single calibration window) yields a 1.6× latency reduction and 1.9× LER reduction for the HSD over minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM)—directionally consistent with simulation but quantitatively smaller, indicating noise sources beyond the model. This pilot exercises the HSD alone: the SCE and the OCL have not been run on physical hardware, and the three modules have never been executed jointly on a device. The end-to-end QCOP benefits—speed-up, energy error reduction and variance reduction—are therefore not hardware-validated, and end-to-end hardware validation of all three modules remains future work. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/hekimoghlu/QCOP.
nf33364b8015d: The synthesis of monolayer graphene has progressed from exfoliation to bottom-up strategies, enabling increasing atomic-level control. This review compares key routes, chemical vapour deposition (CVD), SiC epitaxy, arc discharge, molecular assembly and single-atom catalysts (SACs) and evaluates their mechanisms, scalability and quality bottlenecks. CVD remains the most mature and scalable approach, delivering centimetre-scale-single-crystal films through optimized substrates, roll-to-roll annealing and dry transfer, yet transfer-induced defects and wafer-scale non-uniformity persist. SiC epitaxy enables transfer-free, wafer-scale graphene with well-aligned domains, but requires high temperatures and costly wafers. Arc discharge offers catalyst-free production of crystalline graphene flakes, although monolayer yield and purity remain limited. Molecular assembly provides unmatched structural programmability and atomic precision in nanoribbons and nanographene islands, typically restricted to micrometre scales and stringent conditions. SAC-mediated growth represents a precision limit, where isolated metal atoms catalyse single-carbon insertion or removal at graphene edges, though current demonstrations remain largely single-event observations. Complementing these routes, artificial intelligence/machine learning is increasingly used for parameter optimization, predictive modelling of domain size/uniformity/defects and automated quality control (convolutional neural network/ generative modelling and YOLO-based defect detection). Overall, industrially viable, defect-free monolayer graphene will require combining scalable growth, transfer-free integration, atomic-precision and AI-enabled closed-loop optimization.
na1ff310586e8: Generative agents powered by large language models (LLMs) demonstrate human-like characteristics through sophisticated natural language interactions. Their ability to assume roles and personalities based on predefined character biographies has positioned them as cost-effective substitutes for human participants in social science research. This paper explores the validity of such persona-based agents1 in representing human populations; we recreate the HEXACO personality inventory experiment by surveying 310 GPT-4 powered agents, conducting factor analysis on their responses, and comparing these results to the original findings presented by Ashton et al. (Ashton et al. 2004 J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 87, 707–721 (doi:10.1037/0022-3514.87.5.707). Our results found (i) a coherent and reliable personality structure was recoverable from the agents’ responses demonstrating partial alignment to the HEXACO framework, (ii) the derived personality dimensions were consistent and reliable within GPT-4, when coupled with a sufficiently curated population, and (iii) cross-model analysis revealed variability in personality profiling, suggesting model-specific biases and limitations. We discuss the practical considerations and challenges encountered during the experiment. This study contributes to the ongoing discourse on the potential benefits and limitations of using generative agents in social science research and provides useful guidance on designing consistent and representative agent personas to maximize coverage and representation of human personality traits, while highlighting potential limitations of applying human psychometric frameworks to generative agents.
neb1570ec24da: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children’s, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.
n05c6c4984c30: In human language, word order impacts how words are categorized and understood (as nouns, verbs etc.). We have demonstrated that this effect extends to non-linguistic stimuli, suggesting that the impact of sequence order on stimulus categorization is a domain-general, rather than language-specific cognitive process. Here, we ask if this process is evolutionarily conserved in other non-human primates. We developed a non-linguistic experiment and tested rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and bonobos (Pan paniscus). Participants first learned to categorize shapes (as rounded, squared or pointed). We next assessed how they categorized ambiguous morph shapes by combining exemplars from each category. We provided sequential information by training the animals to select shapes in a specified order: rounded, then squared and then pointed. Finally, we assessed whether presentation in specific positions in this learned sequence would impact subsequent categorization of ambiguous morph shapes. In humans, an ambiguous morph was more likely to be categorized as the shape it replaced in a sequence. Non-human primates, however, showed no such effect, categorizing stimuli independent of their position in a sequence. This suggests that the tendency to infer category membership from sequence order is not shared across primates, and may have evolved more recently in the human lineage.
nbd05594d8f94: Mirror life presents a low-likelihood but high-severity global biosecurity threat that has attracted the attention of bioscientists, governments and international security organizations.
